prompt: This is an art-direction redesign for Yorimichi, a stylised Japanese autumn exploration game made in Unreal. Image 1 is a real, unretouched screenshot of the game as it is now. Repaint THE SAME VIEW from the same camera, keeping the layout, street grid, terrain, building positions, sea and sky composition, but redesigned to the standard of a polished commercial stylised game (think Ghibli-inspired, hand-crafted, cosy, dense and lived-in): textured materials with soft hand-painted detail instead of flat untextured colour, coherent warm autumn palette, gentle afternoon sunlight. It must stay a believable real-time game frame built from meshes, textures and foliage, not a loose illustration. No text, no UI, no watermark. Far view of the harbour city from the sea. Fix: the city currently reads as a flat, pale, washed-out blue-grey carpet. Give it depth and contrast: warm terracotta, slate-blue and dark-tiled kawara roofs with clear value variation, cream and timber walls, dark shadowed alleys, trees and gardens breaking up the blocks, a stone sea wall and harbour quays with boats. The ground between buildings must not be blank: streets, yards, gardens, small fields. The forested hills behind are a dense, rich autumn forest (deep greens, crimson, amber), with natural atmospheric perspective fading softly into blue haze, not frosted white. Natural sea colour, no visible sea edge.
